decision: Complete the candidate's existing 26-language acceptance set first; additions outside it are deferred to a later version.
acceptance_rule: Every in-scope language must have passing evidence for every required layer before it is labeled FULL_SUPPORT. Recognition fixtures alone do not satisfy full language acceptance.
deferred_note: These examples are not a complete future-language backlog. The current release scope is the pinned 26-language set above; later additions require a separately versioned scope and acceptance plan.
release_claim: Do not claim complete multilingual support until all 26 languages pass all five layers and the independent 50-deck prepublication gate passes.

changes: dominant language is chosen by cross-script semantic units, not raw character share, so a Chinese page with English product terms stays zh
Korean hanja (Han characters inside Hangul text) no longer produces a false Chinese/Korean mixed page
URLs and e-mail addresses are stripped before lexical scoring; a bare link is reported und instead of Portuguese
Latin markers carry everyday content words and allow bounded inflection matching (shoppers/shopping, tuketiciler, anazungumza)
mixed pages report mixed=true with the secondary language when prose evidence exists, not only when a brand name appears
uncertain pages (numbers, emoji, links, proper nouns, very short labels) are reported und/uncertain and listed for pending handling

scene_dedupe.identity_normalization: canonical scene ids are unified on case, separators, repeated underscores and simple English plurals before dedupe
scene_dedupe.audit_trail: semantic scene plans carry dedupe_audit with kept/merged decisions per scene identity
scene_dedupe.distinct_subscenes_preserved: normalization never rewrites the head noun, so supermarket/checkout/receipt sub-scenes stay distinct
